summary: Backend-only regression + full new-feature verification for Garlic by Urban Nest iteration 4 (product search, reviews, Nest Rewards points program, referral bonus, order history/timeline). Created /app/backend/tests/test_reviews_points_orders.py with 29 tests across 8 classes: Regression (root, categories, products, collections, editorials, auth/me), Search (?q= case-insensitive regex + empty result), Reviews (auth-required, rating 1-5 validation, create returns id/user_name/rating/title/body/created_at, upsert dedupe per user, product detail exposes average_rating rounded 1dp + review_count), Points (auth-required, new user 0 balance with rate_per_rupee=0.1 + redeem_value=0.10), Order+Mock-Pay (history 'created' on create, mock-pay awards points = 10% of amount, points_earned in response, transaction with type=earn/reason=order_earn/meta.order_id, idempotent second mock-pay does NOT double-award, 'paid' appended to history), Redemption (spends points immediately, discount = pts*0.10, amount = subtotal - discount, 400 on over-balance, 30% cap actually clips when balance > cap), Referral (public mark-bought without auth awards owner exactly 500 pts on first buy, second buy does NOT re-award), Order Timeline (create → mock-pay → admin shipped → admin delivered yields history[] = ['created','paid','shipped','delivered'] in order with 'at' timestamps). Recursive _id-leak assertion applied to every response (products, reviews, points, order detail, admin editorials, admin order status, public shortlist). Result: 29/29 PASSED in 4.53s.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1063 lines — well above the 700-line split threshold. Recommend splitting into routers/ (auth, products, taxonomy, editorials, shortlists, orders, payments, reviews, points).
Deprecated `@app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown')` still in use (server.py:1020, 1061) — migrate to FastAPI `lifespan` context manager.

Startup still does destructive `db.products.delete_many({})` and `db.editorials.delete_many({})` on every restart (server.py:1038, 1055). This wipes any admin-created products/editorials on `supervisorctl restart backend`. Consider a one-time migration flag or seed-if-empty semantics.

Points redemption on order cancellation is NOT refunded — server.py:902 spends points on order create, but there is no `/orders/{id}/cancel` refund path. If a user cancels a redeemed order, their points are lost. Recommend refund on cancel + on failed payment.
Order status transitions are unvalidated — admin can flip from 'delivered' back to 'created' with no guardrail. Consider a status-machine or forward-only transitions.
Review body/title have no length cap — a user could store multi-MB text. Add `max_length` to Pydantic ReviewIn.
Search `?q=` uses unescaped regex — a value like `.*` or `(a+)+` could enable slow/DoS regex. Use `re.escape` before building the regex (server.py:505).
GET /api/products/{id}/reviews has no pagination — currently caps at 500. Add cursor/offset for high-review products.

average_rating in product-list endpoint is NOT included (server.py:481-507) — only /products/{id} returns it. Shop listings therefore can't show stars without N+1 fetches. Consider aggregating summary into list.
seed_data_creation: Tests self-create ~7 disposable users (TEST_UserA/B/C/Owner/Red/Time_* @garlicnest.com) and 1 shortlist per pytest run for isolation across the xdist parallel workers. Reviews are attached to the seeded sample product but are wiped only on backend restart (product reseed does not clear the reviews collection). Test users are NOT deleted (no admin delete-user endpoint exists) — main agent may consider adding one for cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 4 new features verified: (1) Search via GET /api/products?q=<regex-case-insensitive> — works but note the raw-regex ReDoS risk in critical_code_review_comments. (2) Reviews: GET/POST /api/products/{id}/reviews — POST requires auth, rating must be 1-5, upserts (unique per user/product), product-detail carries average_rating (rounded 1 decimal) + review_count. (3) Nest Rewards: GET /api/points returns {balance, value_rupees, rate_per_rupee=0.1, redeem_value=0.10, transactions[]}. Earn = 10% of paid amount added on /orders/{id}/mock-pay (idempotent). Spend on /orders/create with points_to_redeem; discount = pts*0.10, amount = subtotal - discount, capped at 30% of subtotal. Referral: first mark-bought on a shortlist-share awards owner 500 pts, second is no-op. (4) Order history: /orders/{id} returns history[] with entries {status, at}; entries appended on create, mock-pay, and admin status changes. Products + editorials are reseeded on every backend restart; reviews/points/orders/shortlists survive restarts. Use EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env (already handled via python-dotenv in test file).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no backend bugs found. Two initial test-authoring issues encountered during run 1: (a) TestRedemption.test_redeem_ok assumed user_a would carry a positive balance from TestOrderMockPayAndPoints, but pytest-xdist LoadScopeScheduling puts each class on a separate worker with its own session-scoped fixtures — fixed by farming points inline within TestRedemption. (b) TestRedemption.test_redeem_cap_30_percent farmed with qty=20 which produced balance < 30% cap of a qty=1 order (no clipping possible), so 'assert points_redeemed < bal' failed at equality — fixed by farming with qty=50 so balance decisively exceeds the cap. Both fixes were purely test logic; no server.py change required.
